campaigns.title: A scope that collects nothing is a failure, not a survival

mutants.breaks: an exit code this mapping has never seen defaults to 'nothing objected', so an unrecognised failure mode reads as a finding about the code under test

campaigns.title: A bystander kill does not prove the requirement

mutants.breaks: any test dying certifies the requirement, so a campaign passes on tests it never named

campaigns.title: A kill is not believed until it reproduces without the mutant

mutants.breaks: a permanently red test in scope certifies every requirement it touches, forever

campaigns.title: A report from before the last scheduled run is stale, and stale blocks

mutants.breaks: FR-11's `SHALL treat a missing or stale report as blocking`. A nightly that hangs writes nothing, so yesterday's report is still on disk and the gate answers CLEAR over a run that never happened. Measured 2026-08-20: a wedged 03:00 run reported a clean bill of health at 04:22 and would have every morning after
the opposite, and the one that gets the gate switched off: a report written by tonight's own run blocks anyway, so freshness becomes a second way to fail a clean night and nobody trusts the verdict

corrupt JSON, a zero-byte file or a half-written record all parse to {} and every rule below reads that as nothing to report, so a run killed mid-write reports CLEAR with a fresh timestamp the staleness rule cannot fault
a by-hand run over one campaign writes a record shaped exactly like the nightly's, and the gate judges 51 mutants as though they were 187
silence about coverage is read as a claim of completeness, which accepts exactly the records the rule refuses
a verdict measured over uncommitted work that has since changed still answers, and it names no commit anyone could re-derive it from

mutants.old: if current_tree_sha is None or recorded != current_tree_sha:
mutants.new: if current_tree_sha is not None and recorded != current_tree_sha:
mutants.breaks: a fingerprint that could not be taken passes instead of blocking — the missing measurement counted as a pass
a record naming a commit is refused because somebody started editing, so the gate blocks every morning for a verdict the working tree cannot affect

campaigns.title: A session judged against a red tree is not a clean bill of health

mutants.breaks: the gate stops using the producer's shared name for the record's first block and spells the retired one, so the baseline rule matches no document any producer writes and a red baseline reads as CLEAR — the defect itself, and the reason the name is a constant both sides import
every verdict in a session judged against a tree whose suite never passed is reported as read
a --no-baseline run records {'ran': false}, and dropping the flag turns 'nobody measured' into 'the tree was red' — the gate then blocks every run that never claimed to know
a red baseline that carries no failure count is described as '0 failing', which reads as a green tree in the one place a human looks

campaigns.title: The record fingerprints the tree it measured, both halves

mutants.breaks: the sandbox copies untracked files in, so a diff-only fingerprint says the tree is unchanged while the thing measured is not
